statement: In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.
heath_proof: Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angleBAC right; I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC. For let there be described on BC the square BDEC,and on BA, AC the squares GB, HC; [I. 46] through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE, and let AD, FC be joined. Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA, and at the point A on it, the two straight linesAC, AG not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with AG. [I. 14]  For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH. And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC be added to each;therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C. N. 2]  And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two sides FB, BC respectively,and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4] Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and are in the same parallelsBD, AL. [I. 41] And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41] [But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB. Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the square HC;therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C. N. 2] And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC. Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to thesquares on the sides BA, AC.

1.47
**Statement:** In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.

**Step 1.** Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right. It is to be shown that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA and AC taken together.

**Step 2.** On BC describe the square BDEC, and on BA and AC describe the squares GB (with vertices A, B, F, G) and HC (with vertices A, C, K, H), each described on the side of its base remote from the triangle [1.46]. Through A draw AL parallel to BD [1.31], and let it meet BC at M and DE at L. Join AD and FC [P1].

**Step 3.** Since GB is a square, it is right-angled [D1.22], so the angle BAG is right; and the angle BAC is right by hypothesis. Hence with the straight line BA, and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC and AG, which do not lie on the same side of BA, make the adjacent angles BAC and BAG equal to two right angles. Therefore CA is in a straight line with AG [1.14].

**Step 4.** For the same reason, since the angles CAB and CAH are both right (the latter being an angle of the square HC [D1.22]), the straight lines AB and AH, which do not lie on the same side of CA, make with CA at the point A adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore BA is in a straight line with AH [1.14].

**Step 5.** The angle DBC is right, being an angle of the square BDEC, and the angle FBA is right, being an angle of the square GB [D1.22]; therefore the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA [P4]. Since the squares lie on the sides of BC and BA remote from the triangle, the angle DBA is made up of the angles DBC and CBA, and the angle FBC is made up of the angles FBA and ABC. Adding the angle ABC to each of the equal angles DBC and FBA, the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC [CN2].

**Step 6.** Since BDEC and GB are squares, they are equilateral [D1.22]; so DB is equal to BC and FB is equal to BA. Thus in the triangles ABD and FBC the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two sides FB, BC respectively, and the angle ABD contained by them is equal to the angle FBC [Step 5]. Therefore the base AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC [1.4].

**Step 7.** In the figure BDLM, BD is parallel to ML by construction [Step 2], and BM is parallel to DL, since BC and DE are opposite sides of the square BDEC, which was constructed with its opposite sides parallel [1.46]; hence BDLM is a parallelogram, which we call BL. The parallelogram BL and the triangle ABD have the same base BD and are in the same parallels BD and AL. Therefore the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD [1.41].

**Step 8.** The side FB of the square GB is parallel to the opposite side GA, by the construction of the square [1.46], and GA together with AC forms the single straight line GC [Step 3]. Hence the square GB and the triangle FBC have the same base FB and are in the same parallels FB and GC. Therefore the square GB is double of the triangle FBC [1.41].

**Step 9.** Since the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC [Step 6], the double of the one, being the sum of two equals, is equal to the double of the other [CN2]. The parallelogram BL is equal to the double of the triangle ABD and the square GB is equal to the double of the triangle FBC [Steps 7, 8]; therefore the parallelogram BL is equal to the square GB [CN1].

**Step 10.** Join AE and BK [P1]. Since BD is parallel to CE, these being opposite sides of the square BDEC [1.46], and AL was drawn parallel to BD, AL is also parallel to CE [1.30]. Hence MCEL is a parallelogram (MC being parallel to LE, as in Step 7); call it CL.

**Step 11.** The angle BCE is right, being an angle of the square BDEC, and the angle ACK is right, being an angle of the square HC [D1.22]; therefore they are equal [P4]. Adding the angle ACB to each, the whole angle ACE is equal to the whole angle BCK [CN2]. Since CE is equal to CB and CK is equal to CA [D1.22], the two sides AC, CE are equal to the two sides KC, CB respectively, and the angle ACE is equal to the angle KCB; therefore the triangle ACE is equal to the triangle KCB [1.4].

**Step 12.** The parallelogram CL and the triangle ACE have the same base CE and are in the same parallels CE and AL [Step 10]; therefore the parallelogram CL is double of the triangle ACE [1.41]. The square HC and the triangle KCB have the same base CK and are in the same parallels CK and BH, since CK is parallel to the opposite side HA of the square [1.46] and HA together with AB forms the single straight line HB [Step 4]; therefore the square HC is double of the triangle KCB [1.41].

**Step 13.** Since the triangle ACE is equal to the triangle KCB [Step 11], their doubles are equal [CN2]; therefore the parallelogram CL is equal to the square HC [CN1].

**Step 14.** The straight line ML divides the square BDEC into the two parallelograms BL and CL, and these are equal respectively to the squares GB and HC [Steps 9, 13]. Therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB and HC taken together [CN2].

**Step 15.** Now BDEC is the square described on BC, the side subtending the right angle BAC, while GB and HC are the squares described on BA and AC, the sides containing the right angle. Therefore in the right-angled triangle ABC the square on the side BC subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides BA and AC containing the right angle. Q.E.D.
